classification.difficultyReason: Translate the negative gradient and positive intercept into a descending line crossing the y-axis above the origin, then select the matching sketch.

content.prompt: Which of the following could be the graph of $y=-2x+2$?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13, four graph choices at the bottom of the page
spec.description: Four schematic graphs in one horizontal row, labelled A–D. Each has positive-direction axis arrowheads and a line with arrowheads at both ends. No grid, ticks or numerical labels. Exact unlabelled coordinates are unspecified; drawing coordinates express only the source-supported directions and intercept signs.
spec.mathematics: A: negative gradient, positive y-intercept and positive x-intercept. B: negative gradient, negative y-intercept and negative x-intercept. C: positive gradient, negative y-intercept and positive x-intercept. D: positive gradient, positive y-intercept and negative x-intercept.
spec.answerVisibility: All four options are permanent student-visible givens; no option is highlighted.

answer.worked: The gradient is $-2$, so the line slopes downwards from left to right. The $y$-intercept is $2$, so the line crosses the $y$-axis above the origin. Correct answer: A.
